title: 'Incorruptible institutions can't be built only out of governance design, because law is itself an institution'
summary: Joshua Pritikin, who published Religion Unburdened by Belief this June, writes a 6,000-word review that accepts the diagnosis and then pushes it one level up. He restates the argument accurately — financial gravity as shareholder primacy pulling toward extraction, answered structurally through Costco's governance, Patagonia's ownership and GitLab's values embedded in process — and calls it a good diagnosis. His objection is that every one of those structures is downstream of law: a mission lock is enforceable because statutes make it so, and statutes hold only while the people administering them choose to honour them. He takes recent failures in national governance as evidence, and argues the real leverage point is whether people in power can feel the pull toward self-interest without going under — a capacity he says we have no reliable way to test for.
blockquote: Incorruptible institutions can’t be built only out of governance design, because law is itself an institution. Someone still has to choose to honor it.
